# Privacy First Compress

> Free, open-source image compressor that runs entirely in the web browser. Photos are never uploaded to a server: compression happens on the user's own device. Output keeps the same resolution with near-identical visual quality, and JPEG photos keep their metadata (date taken, camera, GPS location).

Privacy First Compress is for people who want to free up storage without deleting photos and without sending personal pictures to an online service.

## How it works

- Images are drawn onto an HTML canvas and re-encoded in the browser at the chosen quality level (low, medium or high compression).
- The page sets a Content Security Policy with `connect-src 'none'`, so the browser blocks every network request the page could use to send data. Users can confirm this in the browser DevTools Network tab while compressing.
- There are no analytics, no accounts and no server-side processing. Fonts are bundled with the app.
- Many images can be compressed at once and downloaded together as a ZIP file.
- A file is never made larger: if compression does not reduce the size, the original file is returned.
- Example from testing: a 1.57 MB JPEG photo was reduced to 453 KB (72% smaller).

## Formats

- JPEG in: JPEG out, with EXIF metadata (date taken, camera, GPS) preserved. This can be switched off.
- WebP in: WebP out.
- PNG with transparency: WebP out, transparency kept.
- PNG without transparency, BMP and other formats the browser can decode: JPEG out.
- GIF and SVG: returned unchanged.

## Links

- [Live app](https://privacy-first-image-compress.vercel.app): use it in any modern browser, no install or sign-up
- [Source code on GitHub](https://github.com/Krunalio/Privacy-first-image-compress): MIT licensed, built with React
- [README](https://github.com/Krunalio/Privacy-first-image-compress/blob/main/README.md): background, features and how to run it locally
